title: Getting help
lede: Who to contact, in what order, and why you should not open a vendor ticket yourself.

blocks.title: Vendor tickets are filed by OME
blocks.text: If you hit something that looks like an ExamSoft defect, send it to Jesse rather than contacting ExamSoft directly. Tickets filed by OME carry the institution context, the portal edition, and the account details the vendor needs, so they get resolved instead of bouncing back for information.

blocks.caption: Where to take a problem
rows: Cannot sign in, or the account-not-found error
Permissions wrong, or a portal area is missing
Need a category added to the shared tree
Student account, roster, or exam-taker record
Draft handoff, preview, printing, proctor materials
The proctor in the room, immediately
Jesse Thompson, who files the vendor ticket

blocks.title: During an exam, the proctor is the first call
blocks.text: Students are told not to troubleshoot on their own, and the same applies to you. The proctor holds the resume code and the hard copies. Escalation after the fact is fine; improvisation during the exam is not.

blocks.title: Check the title before you trust an article
blocks.text: Searching the support site returns Enterprise and Legacy versions of nearly every article, and they describe different screens. If the title does not start with **Legacy Portal**, or the article is not explicitly marked as covering both, it may not match what you see.
